policy.name: Walton County Fund Balance Policy (Board Resolution 2012-59, effective for fiscal years ending on or after 9/30/2012)
rules: Applies to the General Fund only. Targeted minimum unrestricted fund balance (committed + assigned + unassigned) equals two (2) months of the current year's budgeted operating expenditures and transfers out for the fund. This follows the GFOA recommended minimum of two months.

Reserve for Contingency (also called the Emergency Reserve) is committed fund balance. Once established, money can come out only by a supermajority vote of the Board and three findings: the expense cannot be delayed, no other source of funds exists, and it was unanticipated. The dollar level is set by the Board under Florida statutes (the resolution does not state a number).
Cash Balance Brought Forward is assigned fund balance, used to cover differences between budgeted revenues and expenditures.
If the minimum is not met, the County may not budget unassigned fund balance to balance the budget without Board approval.
Spending order: restricted first, then committed, then assigned, then unassigned.

other_mentions: ACFR MD&A (PDF p.12): since FY2021 the county reports an increase of 31,917,513 in General Fund unassigned reserves and 81,572,670 in administrative and committed tourist development tax reserves (quoted from the report).

ACFR MD&A (PDF p.13): about 46M of tourist tax reserve money has been used to buy beach access/parking property since 2021, and a 60M to 70M beach renourishment project (Seagrove, Blue Mountain, Inlet, Dune Allen; 12.9 miles) is expected to be paid from tourist tax and any federal/state funds.

No separate written minimum reserve policy was found for the Tourist Development, Solid Waste, Transportation or Capital Projects funds (searched the ACFR notes and the county's Financial Policies page https://stories.opengov.com/countyofwaltonfl/published/GGoc5o7sB). Their balances are restricted or assigned by purpose instead.

Fund balance is not the same as cash on hand: it includes receivables and is net of liabilities.
Fine and Forfeiture fund is the Sheriff-funding fund; do not label it 'Sheriff reserves' without the explanation above.
